text: Marta Voss painted Mill Lane every morning for eleven years.
asr: Marta Vass painted Mill Lane every morning for 11 years.

text: Eight houses. One lamp. A pear tree that never bore a pear.
She painted only what she could see. That was the rule.
On a Wednesday, she found a ninth house in her journal. A red door, at the end of the lane. Her own brushwork. Not her memory.
She walked outside. Eight houses. She laughed, and felt foolish.
asr: She walked outside, ate houses, she laughed and felt foolish.

text: On Thursday there were nine. The neighbours said it had always been there.
Each morning, the page held something she had not painted. A light in the window. A table. A woman, bent over a sheet of paper.
On Monday, the woman looked up.
Marta crossed the lane. Behind her, her own house began to fade to paper.
asr: Mara crossed the lane. Behind her, her own house began to fade to papers.

text: In eleven years, she never once asked who was painting Marta Voss.
asr: In 11 years, she never once asked who was painting Mara Vass.
